label: Gulf regulators
summary: Regimes where the regulator, not the organisation, decides whether and how the rules bind: NCA (ECC and its cloud, data, OT and telework extensions), SAMA, UAE IA, QCB and Abu Dhabi health (ADHICS, Malaffi). Onboarding records the legal basis, the accountable executive, whether cyber is independent of IT, outside approvals for cloud and outsourcing, and how results are assessed.

source.ref: Each regulator's own scope text: the regulator, not the organisation, decides whether and how its regime binds the entity

fields.label: Applicability basis
options: Owns, operates or hosts critical national infrastructure

source.ref: NCA ECC-2:2024 scope (English PDF read) and NCNICC-1:2025 for private entities outside critical national infrastructure, as reported by Baker McKenzie and CMS (nca.gov.sa unreachable)

fields.note: ECC applies to government bodies and affiliates and to private owners or operators of critical national infrastructure (CNI); NCA encourages others. Other private entities fall under NCNICC-1:2025 (law-firm reports, not read). NCA decides who is designated.

fields.label: Designation reference

when.eq: Owns, operates or hosts critical national infrastructure

source.ref: ECC-2:2024 names private owners or operators of critical national infrastructure; how a designation is issued and referenced was not found

fields.note: Reference of the letter or decision by which NCA or the sector regulator named the entity as critical national infrastructure. How it is issued and numbered was not found (unverified); record what the entity holds.

fields.label: Cloud role

source.ref: NCA Cloud Cybersecurity Controls CCC-2:2024: separate provider and tenant controls, each tagged P or T (English PDF on cdn.nca.gov.sa, read)

fields.note: CCC-2:2024 sets different controls for cloud service providers and for tenants (each control is tagged P or T). Record the role the entity plays; Neither means CCC has nothing to cover.

fields.label: Cloud level

source.ref: CCC-2:2024 has four levels tied to the classification of tenant data (read); the exact level names, renamed in 2024, were not confirmed

fields.note: CCC controls follow four levels tied to the classification of the tenant's data. Level names were renamed in 2024 and were not confirmed (unverified), so match them to NCA's current document and the entity's data classification.

fields.label: Runs OT

source.ref: NCA Operational Technology Cybersecurity Controls (annex PDF read): facility levels L1 to L3

fields.note: OTCC covers industrial control and other operational technology. Record whether the entity runs any; if not, OTCC has nothing to cover.

fields.label: OT facilities

source.ref: NCA OTCC (annex PDF read): facility level L1 to L3 from NCA's Facility Level Identification Tool; a facility takes the level of its most critical system

fields.note: List each OT facility with its level, L1 to L3, from NCA's Facility Level Identification Tool. A facility takes the level of its most critical system. NCA's tool decides the level, not the entity.

fields.label: Remote work

source.ref: NCA Telework Cybersecurity Controls (PDF read; scope wording not re-checked)

fields.note: Record whether staff work remotely on the entity's systems. NCA's Telework Cybersecurity Controls only matter if they do; NCA or the sector regulator says when they are required.

fields.label: DCC basis
options: Required by NCA or a sector regulator
Required by a client or contract

source.ref: NCA Data Cybersecurity Controls: the PDF was fetched but its text could not be extracted, so scope and levels were not read

fields.note: The scope and levels of NCA's Data Cybersecurity Controls could not be read (the PDF text was not extractable; unverified). Record who requires them, since that party sets the scope.

fields.label: Member category

source.ref: SAMA Cyber Security Framework on the SAMA rulebook: member organisations are banks, insurance and reinsurance, finance companies, credit bureaus, market infrastructures and payment systems

fields.note: SAMA's framework applies to its member organisations. Banks carry extra requirements; other members have some exceptions. SAMA decides membership, so choose Other and ask SAMA if the category is unclear.

fields.label: Exceptions checked

source.ref: SAMA CSF: exceptions for non-bank members in sections 3.2.3, 3.3.12 and 3.3.13

fields.note: Non-bank members have exceptions in sections 3.2.3, 3.3.12 and 3.3.13 of the framework. Tick when the entity has checked which of them apply.

fields.label: Target maturity

source.ref: SAMA CSF maturity scale 0 Non-existent, 1 Ad-hoc, 2 Repeatable but informal, 3 Structured and formalized, 4 Managed and measurable, 5 Adaptive; members operate at 3 or higher (read and checked)

fields.note: SAMA expects members to operate at maturity level 3 or higher on its 0 to 5 scale. Choose the level the programme aims at overall; banks must reach level 4 in some areas (next question).

fields.label: Maturity today
fields.note: The maturity level of the last assessment on SAMA's 0 to 5 scale. It is the baseline the target is measured from.

fields.label: Last assessed
fields.note: Date of the last maturity assessment, if there was one.

fields.label: Level 4 areas

source.ref: SAMA circular 298140000067 of 17 January 2019 to banks: maturity level 4 in event, incident, threat and vulnerability management (as stated on the rulebook page)

fields.note: A SAMA circular of 17 January 2019 asks banks for maturity level 4 in event, incident, threat and vulnerability management. Tick the areas the plan will take to level 4.

fields.label: Applicability basis

source.ref: KPMG UAE paper on UAE IA v2.1 (a bold step towards cyber resilience): applies to federal ministries and authorities, non-government CII operators, emirate government entities and emirate CII; the standard's own text and csc.gov.ae were unreachable

fields.note: A KPMG paper says UAE IA v2.1 covers federal bodies, emirate government entities and operators of critical information infrastructure (CII). The standard text was not read. The authority overseeing the entity decides.

fields.label: Sector regulator

source.ref: UAE IA v2.1 text and UAE government portals were unreachable; which body issues the applicability instruction was not confirmed

fields.note: The authority or sector regulator that oversees the entity and can say whether and how UAE IA binds it. Which body issues the instruction was not confirmed (unverified).

fields.label: CII status

source.ref: UAE IA v2.1 text and UAE government portals were unreachable; how critical information infrastructure is designated was not confirmed

fields.note: Whether the authority has designated the entity as critical information infrastructure. The authority decides and how it designates was not confirmed (unverified). Choose Ask the regulator if unsure.

fields.label: Scope confirmation

source.ref: UAE IA v2.1 text and UAE government portals were unreachable; whether the authority issues a written scope statement was not confirmed

fields.note: A written statement from the authority on which controls bind the entity avoids guessing. Whether the authority issues one to every entity was not confirmed (unverified); ask for it.

fields.label: Risk assessment done

source.ref: KPMG UAE paper on UAE IA v2.1: 70 always-applicable and 64 risk-based controls out of 134

fields.note: UAE IA v2.1 is reported to have always-applicable controls plus risk-based ones (70 and 64 of 134, per a KPMG paper). The entity's risk assessment is what is used to choose the risk-based set.

fields.label: Standard version

source.ref: KPMG UAE paper (v2.1, 134 controls) and securityscientist.net (v1.1, 188 controls)

fields.note: Consultancies report 134 controls in v2.1 and 188 in v1.1. Never mix control counts between versions. Ask the overseeing authority which version it holds the entity to.

fields.label: Entity type

source.ref: QCB Technology Risks Regulation for banks (January 2018) and Technology Risk Instructions for Financial Services Operators (2022), PDFs from qcb.gov.qa; which instrument binds a payment service provider was not found

fields.note: The Technology Risks Regulation (January 2018) is written for banks; financial services operators have a separate 2022 instruction. Which one binds a payment service provider was not found (unverified); ask QCB.

fields.label: Facility type

source.ref: ADHICS tiers as reported by vendors and consultancies (qualysec.com, enactia.com); doh.gov.ae failed TLS, so the standard was not read and the sources conflict

fields.note: The only published decider found for the tiers is the number of beds, and the sources conflict (unverified). The Department of Health decides which tiers bind a facility.

fields.label: Tiers required

source.ref: ADHICS tiers Basic, Transitional and Advanced as reported by vendors; the bed-count rule is not confirmed by the standard text

fields.note: One source says hospitals of 1 to 20 beds need Basic and Transitional, and larger hospitals and insurers need all three; sources conflict (unverified). Tick the tiers the Department of Health told you.

fields.label: Tier confirmed

source.ref: ADHICS tiers as reported by vendors; doh.gov.ae unreachable

fields.note: The Department of Health decides the tier. A written confirmation settles the conflict between the published sources (unverified).

fields.label: ADHICS version

source.ref: Vendor claim that ADHICS version 2.0 took effect in August 2024; not confirmed by DoH

fields.note: Version 2.0 is reported effective from August 2024 by vendors only (unverified). Record the version the Department of Health holds the facility to.

fields.label: Connection duty

source.ref: Malaffi operator pages (malaffi.ae): all DoH-licensed facilities must connect unless exempt; licence renewal is blocked when not connected
source.asked_by: Malaffi, Department of Health Abu Dhabi

fields.note: Malaffi's operator says every DoH-licensed facility must connect unless exempt, and licence renewal is blocked for facilities that are not connected. The Department of Health grants exemptions, not the facility.

fields.label: Accession signed

source.ref: Malaffi operator pages: prerequisites are an Accession Agreement and a Facility Declaration

fields.note: Tick when the Accession Agreement and the Facility Declaration, the first prerequisites listed by the operator, are signed.

fields.label: Security assessment

source.ref: Malaffi operator pages: a security assessment, an excerpt of the ADHICS survey, is a prerequisite

fields.note: Tick when the security assessment, an excerpt of the ADHICS survey, has been submitted to the operator.

fields.label: HL7-capable EMR

source.ref: Malaffi operator pages: the electronic medical record system must support HL7

fields.note: Tick when the facility's electronic medical record system can exchange HL7 messages, a prerequisite listed by the operator.

fields.label: Network link

source.ref: Malaffi operator pages: connection over an Etisalat SD-WAN link

fields.note: Tick when the secure network link is in place. The operator's pages name an Etisalat SD-WAN link.

source.ref: Regulator texts on the accountable executive, independence of the cyber function and committee oversight

fields.label: Authorized Official

source.ref: NCA ECC-2:2024: the Authorized Official owns the cybersecurity programme and receives the independent review results (English PDF read)

fields.note: ECC names an Authorized Official who owns the cybersecurity programme and receives the independent review results. Record who holds the role at the entity.

fields.label: Accountable executive

source.ref: Accountability to the board and the regulator is common to these regimes; no single title was confirmed in the texts read

fields.note: The senior executive answerable to the regulator and the board for this programme. Titles differ by regulator and were not confirmed (unverified), so record the person your board or management chose.

fields.label: Head of cyber

source.ref: SAMA CSF (full-time Saudi CISO), NCA ECC-2:2024 (full-time Saudi professionals in the cybersecurity function) and QCB Technology Risks Regulation (CISO reports to an independent governing body)

fields.note: The person who leads cybersecurity. SAMA expects a full-time Saudi CISO; ECC expects full-time Saudi professionals in the cybersecurity function; QCB wants the CISO to report to an independent governing body, not the IT head.

fields.label: Cyber independence
options: Independent of IT, reports to the head of the entity
Independent of IT, reports to a control function

source.ref: ECC-2:2024 (cybersecurity department independent of IT; reporting to the head only recommended), SAMA CSF (independent of IT, reporting to the CEO or managing director or a control-function head), QCB Technology Risks Regulation (CISO not under the IT head)

fields.note: NCA expects cyber to be independent of IT (reporting to the head is only recommended); SAMA wants it independent of IT and reporting to the CEO, managing director or a control-function head; QCB wants the CISO under an independent body, not the IT head.

fields.label: SAMA no-objection

source.ref: SAMA CSF: full-time Saudi CISO appointed with SAMA's no-objection (read and checked)

fields.note: SAMA expects the CISO to be appointed with its no-objection. Record where the request stands.

fields.label: Committee name

source.ref: ECC-2:2024 supervisory committee, SAMA CSF board-mandated cyber security committee, QCB Technology Risks Regulation information security committee

fields.note: ECC expects a supervisory committee, SAMA a board-mandated cyber security committee and QCB an information security committee. Enter its name, or leave empty if there is none.

fields.label: Charter approved

source.ref: Committee requirements in ECC-2:2024, SAMA CSF and the QCB Technology Risks Regulation

fields.note: Date the committee charter was approved by the board or management. Leave empty if there is none yet.

fields.label: Meeting frequency

source.ref: SAMA CSF: the board-mandated cyber committee meets at least quarterly (read and checked)

fields.note: SAMA requires its cyber security committee to meet at least quarterly. Record how often this committee meets.

fields.label: Committee chair

source.ref: SAMA CSF: committee chaired by an independent senior manager of a control function (read and checked)

fields.note: SAMA wants its committee chaired by an independent senior manager of a control function. Name the chair of this committee.

fields.label: Chair independent

source.ref: SAMA CSF: committee chaired by an independent senior manager of a control function (read and checked)

fields.note: Tick when the chair is an independent senior manager of a control function, as SAMA requires.

fields.label: Board approval date

source.ref: QCB Technology Risks Regulation for banks (January 2018): board-approved framework and cyber risk appetite

fields.note: QCB expects a board-approved technology risk framework and cyber risk appetite. Enter the date of the board decision; leave empty if not yet approved.

source.ref: SAMA CSF sections 3.4.2 and 3.4.3 (SAMA approval for material outsourcing and for public or hybrid cloud) and the QCB Cloud Computing Regulation (register of cloud arrangements; QCB approval before a Material Arrangement)

fields.label: Cloud or outsourcing
fields.note: Whether any cloud service or outsourced service is in use or planned. SAMA and QCB need their approval for material arrangements, and each regulator decides what is material.

fields.label: Cloud models
fields.note: SAMA needs its approval for public or hybrid cloud and for material outsourcing (sections 3.4.2 and 3.4.3). Tick every model in use or planned.

fields.label: Providers
fields.note: Pick the cloud and outsourcing providers from the organisation's third-party list. Approvals and registers work arrangement by arrangement.

fields.label: Regulator approval
fields.note: SAMA approves material outsourcing and public or hybrid cloud; QCB approves a Material Arrangement before it starts. The regulator decides what is material, so confirm No material arrangement with it.

fields.label: Cloud register
fields.note: QCB's Cloud Computing Regulation (in force 15 April 2024) requires a register of cloud arrangements. Tick when one has been started.

source.ref: How each regulator evaluates and receives results; only NCA's approach was read

fields.label: NCA evaluation

source.ref: NCA ECC-2:2024 evaluation by self-assessment, tool reports and field visits (read); no ECC certificate exists (law-firm reports)

fields.note: NCA evaluates through self-assessment, reports from its tool and field visits, in the way it deems appropriate. Tick what the entity has been told to expect, or Not told yet. No ECC certificate exists (law-firm reports).

fields.label: Assessment mechanism

source.ref: How SAMA, the UAE authorities, QCB and the Department of Health check compliance was not confirmed in the texts that could be read

fields.note: How the regulator checks compliance was not confirmed for these regimes (unverified). Record what the regulator told you; choose Not told yet if it has not said.

fields.label: Independent reviewer

source.ref: NCA ECC-2:2024: independent review or audit, results to the committee and the Authorized Official (English PDF read)

fields.note: ECC expects a periodic independent review or audit, reported to the committee and the Authorized Official. Name the person or firm; they must sit outside the cybersecurity function. For other regimes this is good practice.

fields.label: Results go to

source.ref: NCA ECC-2:2024: independent review results go to the committee and the Authorized Official (English PDF read)

fields.note: ECC requires the results of the independent review to go to the committee and the Authorized Official. Tick every body that receives them.

fields.label: Reporting channel

source.ref: No reporting portal or tool name was confirmed for any of these regulators; NCA's tool name was not confirmed

fields.note: The portal, tool or contact through which results go to the regulator. No channel name was confirmed for these regimes (unverified); record what the regulator told you.

fields.label: Next report due

source.ref: QCB Technology Risks Regulation: annual compliance report signed by the board (read); no submission date found for SAMA or the others

fields.note: Date of the next report or submission the regulator expects. QCB expects an annual board-signed compliance report; no date was found for the others (unverified), so use the date you were given.

fields.label: Last ECC check
fields.note: Date of the last compliance assessment against the NCA controls, if any.

fields.label: Last result
fields.note: The result of that assessment in a few words, for example the compliance percentage reported.

values: Independent of IT, reports to the head of the entity

gate.label: SAMA's no-objection to the CISO is requested
